mathematics.independent_solution: Choose unit-normal coordinate t with alpha:t=0. Plane distance is |t|. For l>0, |t|=l iff t=l or t=-l (two full parallel planes); |t|<l iff -l<t<l (open slab of thickness 2l, containing alpha); |t|>l iff t>l or t<-l (union of two open exterior half-spaces, no boundary). Thus the complete true set is A,D,E.

option_checks.evidence: -l<t<l is an open slab of normal thickness 2l. It includes t=0 and excludes t=+/-l.
A point at t=l and its reflected point at t=-l both have distance l. Choosing only one side omits an entire valid plane.
Closed exterior half-spaces include points at t=l or t=-l, whose distance is exactly l and therefore not greater than l.
|t|=l has exactly both signed levels t=l and t=-l. Because l>0 they are distinct parallel planes on opposite sides.
|t|>l is t>l or t<-l, precisely both open exterior half-spaces; neither boundary level is admitted.
Every point of alpha has distance 0<l, so removing alpha excludes valid members of the required less-than locus.
